what_its_for: Canakinumab is used to treat certain inflammatory conditions caused by your immune system overreacting. These include a group of rare diseases called periodic fever syndromes (such as CAPS, TRAPS, HIDS, and FMF), as well as a type of arthritis in children called systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis (sJIA), and adult-onset Still's disease (AOSD). It works by blocking a protein in your body called interleukin-1 beta (IL-1β) that causes swelling, pain, and fever.
how_to_take: Canakinumab is given as a shot (injection) under your skin (subcutaneous injection). Your doctor or nurse will give you the first injection in a clinic. After proper training, you or a caregiver may be able to give the injections at home. Common injection sites include the upper arm, thigh, or belly area. Rotate injection sites each time to avoid skin irritation. Do not inject into skin that is red, bruised, tender, or hard. The medicine comes as a pre-filled syringe or as a powder that must be mixed before use — follow your healthcare provider's specific instructions carefully.
dosing: Your dose depends on your specific condition, your weight, and your age. For most adults and children with periodic fever syndromes, a typical starting dose is 150 mg every 8 weeks, but your doctor may adjust this based on how well your symptoms are controlled. For children with sJIA, the dose is usually based on body weight and given every 4 weeks. Always follow the exact dose and schedule your doctor prescribes. Never change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, give the injection as soon as you remember. Then continue on your regular schedule. Do not double up your dose to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist for guidance.
storage: Store canakinumab in the refrigerator at 36°F to 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Keep it in the original box to protect it from light. Do not freeze it, and do not shake the vial or syringe. Once prepared (if mixing the powder form), use it right away or within 24 hours if kept in the refrigerator. Keep out of reach of children. Do not use if the liquid looks cloudy, discolored, or contains particles.
what_to_avoid: Avoid receiving live vaccines (such as MMR, chickenpox, or nasal flu spray) while taking canakinumab, as this medication weakens part of your immune system and live vaccines could cause infection. Talk to your doctor before getting any vaccine. Avoid close contact with people who are sick or have infections whenever possible. Avoid starting this medication if you have an active infection — always tell your doctor if you feel unwell before your injection.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you have: signs of a serious infection such as high fever, chills, cough, difficulty breathing, burning when urinating, or a wound that will not heal; signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing; unusual bruising or bleeding; extreme tiredness or weakness; or any new or worsening symptoms. Also contact your doctor if your condition is not improving or is getting worse.
when_it_works: Many patients begin to notice improvement in their symptoms such as reduced fever, less pain, and less swelling within a few days to a couple of weeks after starting treatment. However, it may take a few months to see the full benefit of the medication. Keep taking it as prescribed even if you feel better, because stopping suddenly can cause your symptoms to return.
special_populations: Children: Canakinumab can be used in children as young as 2 years old for certain conditions, with doses adjusted based on body weight. Pregnant or breastfeeding women: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The safety of this medication during pregnancy is not fully known, so your doctor will weigh the risks and benefits. Older adults: No special dose adjustment is typically needed for older patients, but they should be monitored closely for signs of infection. Patients with infections or weakened immune systems: This medication should be used with caution. Tell your doctor about all past and current infections, including tuberculosis (TB).
